supersedes.reason: Remove external AgentMux receipt and repin requirements from unstarted release tasks, consume only ctxmux-owned Phase 1 and Recoverable Stop evidence, and make the current upstream dependency explicit.

tasks.title: Prove public-API fork composition
tasks.objective: Build one deliberately small fork-and-combine example using only public APIs without moving scheduling or evaluation into ctxmux.
tasks.outcome: A client can express a bounded Crucible- or MapReduce-like workflow while the runtime remains a mux rather than a Harness.
acceptance: The example creates, forks, observes, stops, and combines Runs using only public client and Integration APIs.
Scheduling, evaluation, reduction, winner selection, and stopping policy remain inside the example client.
The example is deterministic enough for the repository gate and does not create a reusable orchestration framework.

verification.proves: The public composition example and full repository checks pass.

tasks.title: Prepare reproducible installation and release gates
tasks.objective: Make binaries and packages installable and release-checkable with public claims bounded to proven behavior, without publishing externally.
tasks.outcome: Ctxmux is release-ready through reproducible local checks and accurate installation and compatibility documentation.
acceptance: Rust binaries and the TypeScript package have reproducible build, install, package-content, and compatibility checks.
README and package metadata distinguish current native, fork, persistence, and tmux guarantees accurately.
Release preparation performs no registry publish, Git push, hosted release, or other external mutation without explicit authorization.

verification.proves: Packaging, installation, compatibility, composition, and full repository checks pass.
Public positioning and installation guidance describe only shipped capabilities.

tasks.title: Consume and qualify Phase 1 local Runtime activation
tasks.objective: Consume the TypeScript activation helper owned by Feature f-22ecztapc and independently qualify it through ctxmux public artifacts instead of implementing another launcher or requiring an external product receipt.
tasks.outcome: A clean ctxmux consumer can reuse or spawn the exact compatible daemon, prove readiness and Hello identity agreement, exit without killing the daemon-owned Run, and reconnect through the public SDK.
acceptance: Feature f-22ecztapc delivers the framework-neutral activation helper and standalone clean-environment evidence before this task begins; release work creates no second helper, alias, launcher, or fallback.

A clean consumer installs only the ctxmux SDK and matching binaries, then proves healthy-daemon reuse, spawn, readiness-to-Hello identity agreement, launcher exit, Run survival, reconnect, and client-only disposal through public APIs.

Fake endpoints, wrong protocol or capability peers, readiness identity mismatch, stale paths, ordinary files, symlinks, permissions, timeouts, and handshake failure fail closed; failed activation cleans up only the child it spawned.
Activation performs no silent download, global configuration mutation, credential handling, product-private directory selection, SSH deployment, runtime fallback, or private daemon access.
The ctxmux Phase 1 owner receipt and ctxmux-owned clean-consumer evidence are sufficient; no external repository pin, receipt, or repin is required.

verification.proves: The release tree consumes the qualified activation surface without duplicating it and keeps repository gates green.
The ctxmux Phase 1 owner has delivered and qualified the activation helper before release consumption.

tasks.title: Complete ctxmux-owned release qualification
tasks.objective: Independently review release-facing claims and execute clean-consumer, supported-platform, security, package, and release gates using exact ctxmux owner evidence without absorbing upstream implementation or downstream product work.
tasks.outcome: The ctxmux release candidate has an auditable public-claim map and reproducible platform evidence with no open release-blocking P0/P1 finding or external-repository acceptance dependency.
acceptance: The exact candidate consumes complete owner evidence from Feature f-22ecztapc and the qualified `native.recoverable_stop` contract from Feature f-22gcz4t8v before release qualification begins.

Independent reviewers cover CLI, SDK, composition, activation, installation, packaging, documentation, security, supported platforms, and release automation; every in-scope P0/P1 finding receives an executable regression and re-review.
Required clean-consumer, platform, package-content, compatibility, security, and release lanes pass without hidden skips, retries, compatibility shims, or external product repositories.
The final report distinguishes Kernel, tmux, Phase 1, Recoverable Stop, and peer-performance owners and does not make unfinished outcomes release evidence.
Before package metadata claims a license or publishability, the user explicitly selects a project license; LICENSE, Rust and SDK metadata, package contents, and install checks then agree.
No registry publish, Git push, hosted release, credential use, or external mutation occurs without explicit authorization.

verification.proves: Required clean-consumer, platform, security, package, and release lanes pass together.
Release review coverage, owner evidence, findings, platform results, and residual limits are auditable.
Recoverable Stop is complete before release qualification consumes the capability.
